crop: Centred square crop covering the tile.

prompt: Image 1 is the Seam material identity. Image 2 is the clean study's dark slate paint crop; image 3 is the palette, with the district triple first. Match the style, proportions and finish of the attached anchors. Generate a single opaque edge-to-edge square game ground texture at the largest native square resolution, strictly overhead orthographic. This variation must visibly read as a flush slate repair mosaic. Two or three broad unequal flat stone pieces abut with staggered, dogleg joints, some partly cut off by the image edges. Dark desaturated green chisel wear along a few of those joints, 8–14 sRGB luma steps below the stone and around 24 pixels wide on a 1254 px canvas at its broadest. Subtle speckled aggregate inside a repair. Keep joints broken and staggered, ornamental lattice absent. Broad matte hand-painted gouache finish, fine paint grain, sparse ink only at material edges. Keep the base plane even across the square, in chromatic green slate between #253235 and #55625E with restrained mineral patina based on #BC9273. Stone pattern should be recognizable when downscaled to 51 pixels; the short, darker lines come from the material, with no directional shading. Keep large color masses equal-valued and quiet across center and edges. Lit by the scene's upper-left key elsewhere: render this material under even diffuse exposure without a cast shadow, shimmer, rim light, bright spots, amber lighting, center glow or vignette. The perspective, colours and old slate finish match the references, while the physical stone topology is the distinct variation described above. No text, letters, numbers, UI, frames, arrows, grid lines, reach dots, HP, targeting rings, watermark, objects, figures or cutout.
